text:
eva: FYI - starting ~09:05 UTC we saw a sustained ~35-45% throughput drop on the us-west runtime pool. latencies spiked and error 504s increased.

sam: saw multiple GPU OOM events in the runtime logs around the same window. worker restarts jumped.

lucy: pulling profiler traces now. early signal: kernel selector started choosing FP32 kernels for a subset of shards at ~09:06 (fallbacks after failed quantized kernels).

ryan: interesting — runtime logs show repeated allocation failures: 
```
AllocationError: failed to allocate 2.1GB tensor on gpu:0 (cudaMalloc)
backtrace: runtime/kernels/select.cpp:243
```
followed by worker recycle.

morgan: noisy-tenant metrics show bursty large-batch jobs hitting same pool at 09:04-09:06. batch size distribution shifted to the right.

sam: also grabbed dmesg: 
```
[09:07:12] Out of memory: Killed process 4321 (runtime-worker) total-vm:123456kB, anon-rss:98765kB
```

sre-oncall: deploy-bot reports 5 worker restarts across nodes runtime-1..runtime-4 between 09:06-09:08. probably cascading.

lucy: profiler flamegraphs show that when fallback to FP32 kernels occurred, peak memory per-shard rose ~25% (no change in sequence length). suggests kernel selection + quantization miss.

eva: does KV cache behavior factor? we saw KV cache retention spike earlier this week after the new prompt-preserve change.

ryan: yes — KV cache size histogram shows a long tail: many requests keep large prefixes pinned; combined with larger kernel memory this pushes allocations over the limit and fragments device heap.

morgan: fragmentation hypothesis confirmed by ```pmap```-style allocation map from our allocator: many small free blocks interspersed with large allocations; subsequent cudaMalloc fails despite "free" bytes reported.

sam: summary of root causes so far: (1) kernel selector fallback to higher-memory FP kernels for some partitions, (2) increased KV cache retention causing larger live allocations, (3) bursty noisy-tenant large batches causing transient pressure -> fragmentation -> cudaMalloc failures -> worker restarts.

lucy: repro steps I used: 1) pin model variant with quantization disabled on node, 2) send mixed sequence length load with ~20% large prefixes, 3) observe kernel selector metrics and allocation failures. Provided profile attached to internal perf-s3.

ryan: short-term mitigations applied at 09:20: 
- scaled down max batch size on us-west pool by 30%
- enabled stricter KV cache eviction for ephemeral prefixes
- restarted affected workers with a 2min backoff to flush fragmentation

deploy-bot: runtime service: restarted workers [runtime-2, runtime-3] (reason: OOM recovery)

sre-oncall: after mitigation we saw throughput recover ~80% of baseline by 09:35; no new OOMs recorded since.

morgan: long-term fixes proposed: 
- improve kernel selector to prefer lower-mem kernels under fragmentation pressure (add memory headroom signal),
- pre-allocation / slab allocator to reduce fragmentation,
- more aggressive per-tenant QoS to prevent noisy neighbor large-batch spikes,
- KV cache LRU tuning to avoid long-tail retention for small tenants.

eva: follow-ups: lucy/ryan to file perf bug with traces and candidate kernel-selector patch (ETA EOD). sam/sre to track worker restart counts in dashboard and alert on OOM vs other restarts. morgan to schedule QoS rollout for next week.

lucy: attaching minimal reproducer snippet in thread: 
```python
# send mixed prefixes to reproduce memory growth
for i in range(2000):
    seq = random.choice([64, 1024])
    client.generate(model='redwood-large', seq_len=seq, prefix=long_prefix_if_needed())
```

sam: thanks — capturing as incident ticket INF-2026. tagging oncall rotation. :thumbsup:

eva: closing loop for now, will reopen if OOMs recur. great cross-team triage. :heart:
